questions.question: If Seema invests ₹17,650 in an account that yields 8.5% p.a. simple interest, then how much (to nearest ₹) will she have after 5 years?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total amount = ₹17,650

The rate of interest = 8.5%

**Formula used:**

S.I. = (P × R × T)/100

Where, S.I. = Simple interest; P = Total amount; R = Rate of interest; T = Time (years)

**Calculation:**

The total amount = Total simple interest + Total invested amount

= [(17650 × 8.5 × 5)/100] + 17650

= 7501.25 + 17650

= ₹25151.25

= ₹25151 (to nearest ₹)

**∴ Seema will have ₹25151 after five years.**

questions.question: The simple interest on a certain sum at the rate of 12.5% per annum for 6 years is Rs. 13,500 less than the principal. Find the simple interest.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Simple interest (S.I) = (principal - 13500)

Rate = 12.5%; time = 6 years

**Formula used:**

S.I = (P × R × T)/100

Where, P = principal; R = rate; T = time;

**Calculation:**

⇒ S.I = (P × R × T)/100

⇒ (P - 13500) = (P × 12.5 × 6)/100

⇒ (P - 13500) = (3/4) × P

⇒ 4P - (13500 × 4) = 3P

⇒ 4P - 3P = 54000

⇒ P = Rs.54000

Simple Interest (S.I) = (P - 13500)

⇒ (54000 - 13500) = Rs.40500

**∴ The correct answer is Rs.40500.**

questions.question: A certain sum of money becomes seven times itself when invested at a certain rate of simple interest, in 14 years. How much time (in years, rounded off to 2 decimal places) will it take to become 18 times itself at the same rate?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula for Simple Interest multiples: T₂ = [(n₂ − 1) ÷ (n₁ − 1)] × T₁

Given n₁ = 7, T₁ = 14 years, and n₂ = 18.

T₂ = [(18 − 1) ÷ (7 − 1)] × 14 = (17 ÷ 6) × 14

T₂ = (17 × 7) ÷ 3 = 119 ÷ 3 = 39.666... ≈ 39.67

**∴ The correct answer is 39.67 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial sum = P

Amount after 14 years (A₁) = 7P

Target Amount (A₂) = 18P

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (I) = Amount − Principal

Simple Interest (I) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
 
 
 P
 7P
 14 Years
 Interest = 6P
 
 
 
 P
 18P
 T = ? Years
 Interest = 17P
 Rate (R) is constant in both cases

**Calculations:**

**Case 1:**

⇒ Interest (I₁) = 7P − P = 6P

⇒ 6P = (P × R × 14) ÷ 100

⇒ R = (6P × 100) ÷ (14 × P) = 600 ÷ 14 = 300 ÷ 7 %

**Case 2:**

⇒ Interest (I₂) = 18P − P = 17P

⇒ 17P = (P × R × T₂) ÷ 100

⇒ 17P = [P × (300 ÷ 7) × T₂] ÷ 100

⇒ 17 = (3 × T₂) ÷ 7

⇒ T₂ = (17 × 7) ÷ 3 = 119 ÷ 3

⇒ T₂ = 39.666... years

⇒ T₂ ≈ 39.67 years

**∴ The correct answer is 39.67 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Relation for Simple Interest Multiples

If a sum becomes 'n' times itself in 'T' years at simple interest, the rate of interest is given by R = [(n − 1) × 100] ÷ T.

Simple vs Compound Interest Concept

In Simple Interest, the interest remains constant for each year. In Compound Interest, the interest gets added to the principal and acts as the new principal for the next period.

Rule of 72

A general estimation trick used in finance: to find the approximate number of years it takes to double your money at a given compound interest rate 'R', divide 72 by R.

questions.question:
A sum of money becomes three times of itself at the rate of 10 percent per annum on simple interest. Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?

I. It will become 5 times of itself at the rate of 20 percent per annum on simple interest in the same time period.

II. It will become 7 times of itself at the rate of 30 percent per annum on simple interest in the same time period.
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

The formula for simple interest is:

I = PRT/100,

where:

I = interest earned,

P = principal amount (initial investment),

R = annual interest rate (in percentage),

T = time (in years).

If a sum of money becomes three times of itself at a rate of 10 percent per annum, it means that twice the initial sum was earned as interest (because the initial sum plus twice the sum gives three times the sum). So:

2P = PRT/100

Substituting the given R = 10, we get:

2P = P × 10 × T/100

Solving for T:

T = 2 × 100/10 = 20 years.

Now, for the two statements:

I. For the money to become 5 times of itself at the rate of 20 percent per annum in the same time period (20 years), the interest earned must be four times the principal. So:

4P = P × 20 ×T/100 = P× 20 × 20/100 = 4P.

So, Statement I is correct.

II. For the money to become 7 times of itself at the rate of 30 percent per annum in the same time period (20 years), the interest earned must be six times the principal. So:

6P = P × 30 × T/100 = P × 30 × 20/100 = 6P.

So, Statement II is also correct.

Thus, both statements I and II are correct.

questions.question: A man borrowed a certain sum of money at the rate of 10% per annum simple interest for the first three years and 15% per annum simple interest for the period beyond three years. If he pays a total interest of Rs. 2884.50 at the end of 7 years, then the sum of money (in Rs.) that he borrowed is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Interest % = (Rate₁ × Time₁) + (Rate₂ × Time₂)

Total Interest % = (10% × 3) + (15% × (7 − 3)) = 30% + 60% = 90%

Given: 90% of Sum = ₹2884.50

Sum (100%) = (2884.50 ÷ 90) × 100 = 32.05 × 100 = ₹3205

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3205.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First rate (R₁) = 10%, Time (T₁) = 3 years

Second rate (R₂) = 15%, Time (T₂) = 7 − 3 = 4 years

Total Interest = ₹2884.50

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
• Start 3 yrs 7 yrs 10% p.a. 15% p.a. Interest₁ = 30% of P Interest₂ = 60% of P Total Interest (90%) = ₹2884.50

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the borrowed sum be P.

⇒ SI for first 3 years = (P × 10 × 3) ÷ 100 = 30P ÷ 100

⇒ SI for next 4 years = (P × 15 × 4) ÷ 100 = 60P ÷ 100

⇒ Total SI = (30P ÷ 100) + (60P ÷ 100) = 90P ÷ 100

⇒ 90P ÷ 100 = 2884.50

⇒ 0.9P = 2884.50

⇒ P = 2884.50 ÷ 0.9

⇒ P = 28845 ÷ 9 = 3205

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3205.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Variable Rate Simple Interest

When interest rates change over time, the total interest is the sum of interest for each period: Total SI = P × (R₁T₁ + R₂T₂ + R₃T₃ + ...) ÷ 100.

Principal and Amount Relationship

The total amount (A) is the sum of the Principal (P) and the Total Simple Interest (SI): A = P + SI.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

Simple interest is calculated only on the principal amount, whereas compound interest is calculated on the principal plus any accumulated interest from previous periods.

questions.question: A person borrowed some money at the rate of 8% per annum for the first two years, at the rate of 11% per annum for the next three years, and at the rate of 16% per annum for the period beyond five years. If he pays a total interest of ₹21,400 at the end of nine years, how much money did he borrow (round to the nearest unit) ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A person borrowed some money at the rate of 8% per annum for the first two years, at the rate of 11% per annum for the next three years, and at the rate of 16% per annum for the period beyond five years. If he pays a total interest of ₹21,400 at the end of nine years, how much money did he borrow (round to the nearest unit)?

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = P × R × T / 100

Where,

P = Principal amount

R = Rate of interest

T = Time period

**Calculation:**

Let the borrowed amount be P.

Interest for the first 2 years at 8%:

SI₁ = P × 8 × 2 / 100

⇒ SI₁ = 0.16P

Interest for the next 3 years at 11%:

SI₂ = P × 11 × 3 / 100

⇒ SI₂ = 0.33P

Interest for the remaining 4 years at 16%:

SI₃ = P × 16 × 4 / 100

⇒ SI₃ = 0.64P

Total interest paid after 9 years:

SIₜₒₜₐₗ = SI₁ + SI₂ + SI₃

⇒ 21400 = 0.16P + 0.33P + 0.64P

⇒ 21400 = 1.13P

⇒ P = 21400 / 1.13

⇒ P = 18938.0531

⇒ P ≈ ₹18,938

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**

questions.question: A person borrowed Rs. 1760 at 6% per annum and Rs. 2240 at 9% per annum at simple interest for the same period. He had to pay Rs. 1536 in all as interest. Find the time (in years).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal 1 (P₁) = Rs. 1760

Rate 1 (R₁) = 6% per annum

Principal 2 (P₂) = Rs. 2240

Rate 2 (R₂) = 9% per annum

Total Interest = Rs. 1536

**Concept Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = Principal (P) × Rate (R) × Time (T) / 100

**Formula Used:**

SI₁ = P₁ × R₁ × T / 100

SI₂ = P₂ × R₂ × T / 100

Total Interest = SI₁ + SI₂

**Calculation:**

SI₁ = 1760 × 6 × T / 100

⇒ SI₁ = 105.6T

SI₂ = 2240 × 9 × T / 100

⇒ SI₂ = 201.6T

Total Interest = SI₁ + SI₂

⇒ 1536 = 105.6T + 201.6T

⇒ 1536 = 307.2T

⇒ T = 1536 / 307.2

⇒ T = 5

**∴ The time period is 5 years.**

questions.question: In a bank, 6% interest is given on the deposited amount. The bank then invests the money in the stock market and is able to earn ₹30,000 for every ₹3,00,000. How much money is the bank earning finally if the total amount deposited in the bank is ₹60,00,000?

Bank's earning rate from the stock market = (30,000 ÷ 3,00,000) × 100 = 10%

Final earnings of the bank = 4% of 60,00,000

Final earnings = (4 ÷ 100) × 60,00,000 = ₹2,40,000
